sections.overview: The Izu stingray is restricted to Japan’s Izu Peninsula and is currently placed in Hemitrygon. The H. marianae profile shares its former Dasyatis label but is now placed in a different genus.
sections.identification: Its smooth, golden-brown diamond-shaped disc and white ventral tail fold distinguish it from other described Dasyatidae.
sections.habitat: The original specimens came from shallow coastal waters at about 10–20 m off Izu.
sections.diet: The sources consulted provide no species-specific prey list.
sections.behavior: Species-specific activity and social behavior are poorly documented in the sources reviewed.
sections.reproduction: FishBase records the Izu stingray as ovoviviparous.
sections.ecology: Its range is confined to shallow coastal waters around Izu.
sections.conservation: FishBase reports a 2019 IUCN assessment of Vulnerable.
